about: Where the second version of the loader of open-field, v2, and the base change OS 1.7.3+0 of the OP-1 Field, and nothing else: no byte of the firmware is in this file. It is profiles/op1f-1.7.3.json, the profile of the loader v1, with the room for our code and the change of the heap's size made for v2, and two fields more: pack_link and pack_room. The places and the tables are the same. A pack names the places it changes in a profile of its own.
stock_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the firmware file an owner copies off their own unit; every address below belongs to that one file.

patches: each place once. address and length say where it is; sum is the CRC-32 of the firmware's own bytes there, by which the loader knows the place before it changes it; name says in our words what stands there; group is the part of open-field that uses it (image: changed in the file by the builder; every other: changed in the running firmware at the start).

tables: for the loader and for the base (and, in a pack's own profile, for that pack), which function of ours goes to which place. form: a word of data, a call, a jump, or the load of an address. room and copies: the loader copies that many bytes of the instructions the change displaces from the running firmware into the room and puts a jump back behind them. An entry has a sum of its own when its trampoline copies more bytes than the place is long.

image: what the builder changes in the firmware file itself, before anything runs. kind imm32: the number an instruction loads at that address becomes new_imm. kind call: a call of the function target, which is in the loader, over length bytes. module_base and reserved_bytes are the room for the loader alone, 128 KiB at the top of the file's record of zeros: the new heap size makes the heap end at module_base, the loader's first byte. entry is the address the file's first record names, and heap_fill_base and heap_fill_bytes are the file's record of zeros that the room lies in: the builder looks for all three in an owner's file before it changes anything. builder/write-manifest.mjs makes the builder's manifest from these and from a built loader, with --profile profiles/op1f-1.7.3-n2.json. The loader is our small piece inside the firmware file; the base is the pack base.pack, a file on the unit.

pack_link and pack_room, the two fields this profile has and the one of v1 has not. pack_link is the window a pack is linked at, its first address and its bytes, the same window as under v1, so one pack file runs under both loaders. pack_room is where the loader v2 puts the pack files it loads: its first address, its bytes (16 MiB) and the most pack files it looks at (files). The builder holds the room's numbers in the manifest it writes, so the install page can make the same checks.

The table sources in module/ are made from profiles/op1f-1.7.3.json, whose places and tables this file repeats. docs/changes.md is made from this file, the profile of the loader the install page offers.

image.does: The builder makes it 128 KiB smaller, so that the heap ends where the loader begins. The memory that is left over is where the loader is loaded.
